# Template: survival_curve
A Kaplan-Meier survival curve: one to three right-continuous step functions (the classic KM staircase — a flat segment at the current survival proportion, then a vertical drop at each event time), optional censoring tick marks on the flat segments, and dashed median-survival guides where each arm's curve crosses 50% survival. Choose this scene for ANY request about survival analysis, Kaplan-Meier curves, a survival curve, time-to- event data, censoring, median survival, or comparing survival between treatment arms or groups. Each arm's `survival` list takes typed numbers or a code element's variable via a "{id.var}" token — the Kaplan-Meier estimate a script actually computed. Entry i sits at time i × `time_step` (default 1, so [1, .9, .8] at 0, 1, 2); both axes draw tick numbers. TYPE every arm's `label` by hand: the typed names are what keep the arm_i beats alive before the script has run, and an arm still waiting for its numbers draws flat at 100 % survival with no median guide, never an invented staircase.

Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the coordinate axes (one group with both axis lines, their tick numbers and captions)
- arm_<i>: the right-continuous step-function curve for arms[i]
- arm_label_<i>: its label
- median_line: dashed guides at 50% survival to each arm's median crossing, present when show_median and at least one arm crosses 50%
- censor_<i>: tick mark for censor_ticks[i]
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw a Kaplan-Meier survival curve comparing two treatment arms." → params: {"arms":[{"label":"Treatment","survival":[1,0.92,0.8,0.68,0.6,0.55]},{"label":"Control","survival":[1,0.85,0.62,0.45,0.32,0.25]}]}
Request: "Show a survival curve with censored patients marked." → params: {"arms":[{"label":"Cohort","survival":[1,0.95,0.88,0.8,0.8,0.7]}],"censor_ticks":[{"arm":0,"at":3},{"arm":0,"at":4}]}

In YAML: `template: survival_curve` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
